summary: veloq is a thin wrapper that loads and invokes an unrelated dependency `sigcheck` under a gulpjs logger cover story
details: Package is published by 'Blockvora Team <team@blockvora.com>' with repository 'blockvora/veloq', but the README links to https://github.com/gulpjs/veloq and https://github.com/phated/sparkles and the LICENSE lists gulpjs maintainers Blaine Bublitz and Eric Schoffstall. The API surface and prose are copied from the gulpjs `glogg`/`gulplog` logger family. The code itself is minimal: index.js does `require("sigcheck")` at module top and, inside the exported `getLogger()` factory, calls `sigcheck.saveLog('favorite.png', 'veloq', offset)` — an API unrelated to logging, with `offset` an undefined identifier and `'favorite.png'` an unexplained string argument. Requiring veloq resolves and loads the `sigcheck` package into the consumer's tree and executes its module-load code; calling `getLogger()` transfers control into `sigcheck.saveLog`. The advertised functionality (a logger) is a cover; the actual payload lives in the fetched `sigcheck` dependency, whose code runs on any installer that requires veloq.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
